tasks.title: Practical Test 1: Rock / Mineral & Fossil Identification
tasks.statement: IE O 2018 Practical Test 1: Rock / Mineral & Fossil Identification. Time: 50 minutes. Multiple choice questions Q1 through Q18 regarding rock samples, minerals, fossils, and related industrial materials.

tasks.title: Practical Test 2: Field Geology Examination
tasks.statement: Field Geology Examination. In this part of the examination, you will perform measurement at three station (station 1, 2, and 3) indicated in Fig 1. Each student is provided with a Brunton compass. You have 10 minutes per station to perform the measurement. Permissible error in your measurement: a) Full mark for value within +-5 degree of the correct value. b) Half mark for value within 6-10 degree of the correct value. c) No mark for value more than 10 degree away from the correct value.

tasks.title: Practical Test 3: Field Geology Exercise
tasks.statement: Field Geology Exercise. Part I: Calculate true thickness using measurements at three stations in Practical Test 2. Part II: Correlation - use data from Part I to find structure and relative age of the beds.

parts.question: Q10: Calculate the cumulative true thickness of the strata from point X to point Y of Fig 2 using the dip angle from your own measurement in Practical Test 2. You can assume that the apparent thickness of strata from X to Y is 35 meter (see Fig 1). Note that true thickness is measured perpendicular to the bedding plane.
Q11: Choose the option that depict the correct geological profile along line A-B shown in Fig 1.

Q12: Which station has the oldest stratum along the profile A-B?
a) Station 1
b) Station 3
c) Both stations have the same stratum.

tasks.title: Practical Exam Part A & B: Hydrology & Chemistry Pollution
tasks.statement: In this exam there are two sections: Section A and Section B. Students are required to finish the exam within 1.5 hours.

parts.question: Section A - Q1: Use the syringe to measure the increase in water volume. Write this volume on your answer sheet.
Section A - Q2: The density of ice is 0.92 g/cm3, and water is 1.00 g/cm3. Estimate the mass and the volume of ice before melting.
Section A - Q3: Use the syringe to measure the increase in water volume. Write this volume on your answer sheet.

Section A - Q4: From which location will the melting of the ice cap least affect the sea level?
a. The Arctic Ocean
b. Antarctica
c. Greenland

Section A - Q5: If all the ice cap suddenly melted, how much should global sea level rise? Use the average value of the Earth radius (6,371 km) in your calculation. (One correct answer)
a. 100 m
b. 200 m
c. 300 m
d. 400 m
e. 500 m

Section A - Q6: We can also assume that the average depth of all the ocean is about 4,000 m with the average salinity of about 35 part per thousand. What would the ocean salinity be with a great sudden melt down as envisioned in the previous question? Assume the present ocean area is about 70% of the Earth surface.
a. 50 part per thousand
b. 44 part per thousand
c. 34 part per thousand
d. 30 part per thousand
e. 25 part per thousand

Section B - Q7: Put one pack of chromium reagent into each of the water samples. Wait three minutes. Then rank the three samples (a, b, and c) from least to most intense color. Record your answer on the answer sheet.

Section B - Q8: Fig 5 shows the monthly rainfall in the area the samples were collected. Based on the color intensities and the amount of rainfall in each month, indicate in your answer sheet which month each sample was collected.
Section B - Q9: Based on the color intensity from the previous experiment, which factor is the most likely source releasing Cr+6 into the river? (Choose only one answer.)
